name: Mihai Babiac
headline: ML with neuromorphic cameras @ Sony | ETH Zurich | CDTM

positions.title: Student Research Assistant
positions.description: Part of Transport Systems Research Group, worked on implementing state-of-the-art railway delay prediction models based on particle filtering and assumed density filtering.

positions.title: Working Student in FPGA Design
positions.description: As part of the embedded programming team, I worked on offloading compute intensive processing from the software to the FPGA hardware. The result was that the majority of the point cloud post-processing operations were done in the FPGA, leaving headroom for other types of algorithms to be done on the CPU. The work-flow consisted of creating simulations with NumPy in Python, developing the circuits with VHDL and testing them with VUnit, a Python/VHDL unit testing framework, before doing live testing and debugging.

positions.title: Bachelor Thesis "Approximate Computing for Digital Cinema"
positions.description: I investigated how certain mathematical functions can be implemented in FPGAs to provide a tunable accuracy-performance trade-off and how the use of GPUs instead of CPUs influences the results of an image processing pipeline.

positions.title: VHDL Laboratory Tutor
positions.description: I assisted bachelor and master students with learning digital circuit design using VHDL during the "Praktikum VHDL" course.

positions.title: Intern/Working Student Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description: I worked in the Design & Engineering team, developing firmware for a hardware module based on the STM32 family of microcontrollers.

positions.title: Working Student Software Engineer
positions.description: As part of the Indoorviewer team, I integrated an out-of-core point cloud rendering library into the browser-based 3D renderer of the company. The main JavaScript libraries used were Angular.js and Three.js.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description: I contributed to improving the in-house cross-platform game engine. The implementation was in C++ and Lua.
